questions.question: Non-metals generally contain ________ electrons in their outermost shell.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **5,6,7 or 8.**

__**CONCEPT:**__

__
 
• The outermost shell of an electron can accommodate a maximum of 8 electrons.
 
• Elements having filled outermost shell are stable. So all elements tend to attain a stable state by completing its octet.
 
• Elements attain this stable form by losing or gaining electrons.

**EXPLANATION:**__

__
 
• The effective nuclear charge experienced by the outer shell electrons in non-metals is very high.
 
• So they can accept electrons instead of losing electrons. 
 
• Electonic configurations of some non-metals:

 
 

 **Non-metal**
 **Electronic configuration**
 
 

 Oxygen
 2,6

**__Chemical properties of non - metals __**

 
• **Electronic configuration:** Most of the **non - metals have 4 to 7 electrons in their valence shells.**
 
• **Formation of ions:** Non - metals tend to **accept electrons in their valence shell** to form negatively charged ions called **anions.**
 
• **Reaction with oxygen**: Non - metals combine with oxygen to **form their oxides.**

questions.question: What is the radius of an atom used to measure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Atomic size**

**__CONCEPT:__**

__
 
• **Atomic size:** The atomic size depends on the **number of electron orbits** in the atom. The greater the number of orbits the larger the size.

 
 

 
 **Definition**
 
 

 Atomic number
 
 
The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom is the atomic number of that element 

 
It is denoted by the ‘Z’.

 
 
 

 Atomic mass
 
 
The total number of protons and neutron in an atom is the atomic mass number of that element.

 
It is denoted by the symbol ‘A’.

 
 
 

 Atomicity: 
 
 
The number of atoms present in a single molecule is known as atomicity.

 
 
 

**Solution:**__

__
 
• **Atomic radius **is the distance between an atom's nucleus and its valence electrons.
 
• It is measured in Angstroms(Å).
 
• **Atomic radius is used to determine the size of an atom.**
 
• When the atomic radius increases, the size of the atom also increases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e25d6e1cc4ca05f7bcbca45c0cf96f4b69808a54cf9962ba436def16d803ff5c.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In the periodic table, the atomic radius increases down the group and decreases along a period from left to right.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca91a54e65799f678b3f8bf47120fb3a319d5adf7fa456f92d1da636d2154681.png] 

In a group, the biggest atom is found at the bottom and the smallest atom is found at the top.

questions.question: If the valency of Aluminium is 3 and that of Oxygen is 2, then the chemical formula of Aluminium oxide is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **AI2O3.**

**__Concept:__**

__
 
• The **chemical formula** of a compound is an **alphanumeric representation** of the constituents of the compound.
 
• It includes the symbols of the elements present and their respective valencies.
 
• If the valency of an element **A** and element** X **combines together to form a compound and their **valencies are '+a' and '-x' respectively**.
 
• Such a compound is represented by the** chemical formula, AₓXₐ**

**Explanation:__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/836e8d0ba9c0bfb72befd3d1633b414a906515df87e15839bb70f9bbb07649c0.png] 

__
 
• The oxide of aluminum is known as Aluminium oxide.
 
• The valency of aluminum(Al) is +3 and that of oxide is -2.
 
• Therefore, the **chemical formula of aluminum oxide is Al₂O₃**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Metal oxides like aluminium oxide, zinc oxide etc., shows **both acidic as well as basic behaviour.**
 
• **Amphoteric Oxides:**__ The metal oxides which react with both acids as well as bases to produce salts and water.
 
• Aluminium oxide reacts in the following manner with acids and bases:
 
• AI₂O₃ + 6HCl 2AlCl₂ + 3H₂O
 
• AI₂O₃ + 2NaOH → 2NaAlO₂ + H₂O

questions.question: A and B can complete a task in 40 days, B and C can complete it in 30 days while C and A can complete the same task together in 24 days. How many days will each of A, B and C take to complete the task individually?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B complete the task = 40 days.

B and C complete the task = 30 days.

A and C complete the task = 24 days.

 

**Calculation:**

⇒ A + B = 40 days

⇒ B + C = 30 days

⇒ C + A = 24 days

Total work = LCM(40, 30, 24) = 120 units

⇒ (A + B)’s efficiency = 120/40 = 3

⇒ (B + C)’s efficiency = 120/30 = 4

⇒ (A + C)’s efficiency = 120/24 = 5

⇒ (A + B + C)’s efficiency = 12/2 = 6

⇒ A’s efficiency = 6 - 4 = 2

⇒ B’s efficiency = 6 - 5 = 1

⇒ C’s efficiency = 6 - 3 = 3

**A complete the task individually = 120/2 = 60 days.**

**B complete the task individually = 120/1 = 120 days.**

**C complete the task individually = 120/3 = 40 days.**

questions.question: A rectangle having 10 cm and 6 cm as its dimensions was reconstructed to make a rhombus having the same perimeter as that of the rectangle and 60° as one of its angles. The area of the rhombus, in cm², was:
questions.solution:
Given:

Length of rectangle = 10 cm

Breadth of rectangle = 6 cm

Rectangle is reconstructed into Rhombus.

Perimeter of the rectangle is equal to the perimeter of rhombus.

One of the angles of the rhombus is 60°.

 

Concept Used:

Perimeter of Rectangle = 2(L + B)

Perimeter of Rhombus = 4(side)

Area of Rhombus = (side)2 × sin A 

 

Calculation:

Length of rectangle, L = 10 cm

Breadth of rectangle, B = 6 cm

Perimeter of Rectangle = 2(L + B)

⇒ 2(10 + 6)

⇒ 2(16)

⇒ 32 cm

Perimeter of the rectangle = Perimeter of rhombus

⇒ 4(side) = 32

⇒ side = 32/4 = 8 

Area of Rhombus = (side)2 × sin A [where A is any angle of rhombus]

⇒ Area = 82 × sin 60°

⇒ 64 × √3/2

⇒ 32√3 cm2

∴ Area of the rhombus 32√3 cm2.

questions.question: What happens to the ammeter reading when the length of the wire is doubled?
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

Ammeter

__
 
• An Ammeter is a device that is connected to a series of circuits to find the current. 
 
• Ampere is the unit of current. 
 
• Ammeter is connected in series. So, if it is having a high resistance, it will affect the reading as the current will be reduced in the circuit. 
 
• So, an ammeter should have very small (ideally zero) resistance so that perfect reading can be obtained. 
 
• At a given temperature, the resistance (R) of a conductor depends on its length (L), area of cross-section (A), and the material it is made of.
 
• If the length of the wire is doubled then the resistance of the wire will also double. Hence, the Current will decrease to one-half.__

questions.question:
Which of the following signs and numbers should be interchanged such that for the following expression, LHS = RHS.

6 × 4 + 2 = 16
questions.solution:
**Bodmas rule:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f22f57d0cf5c493280a0ab6b7dbaea9e3fc5b035c6d410d59c2f476043bd03a8.png] 

The pattern followed here is:

Let's check each option one by one:

**Option 1) **× with +, 2 with 6

**Given: **6 × 4 + 2 = 16 

After interchanging we get: 

⇒ 2 + __**4 × 6**__ = 16

⇒ 2 + 24 = 16

⇒ 26 ≠ 16 

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

**Option 2) **× with +, 4 with 2

Given: 6 × 4 + 2 = 16 

After interchanging we get: 

⇒ 6 + __**2 × 4**__ = 16

⇒ 6 + 8 =16

⇒ 14 ≠ 16

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

**Option 3) **× with +, 16 with 6

Given: 6 × 4 + 2 = 16 

After interchanging we get: 

⇒ 16 + __**4 × 2 **__= 6

⇒ 16 + 8 = 6

⇒ 24 ≠ 6

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

**Option 4) **× with +, 4 with 6

Given: 6 × 4 + 2 = 16 

After interchanging we get: 

⇒ 4 + __**6 × 2 **__= 16

⇒ 4 + 12 = 16

⇒ 16 = 16

⇒ **LHS = RHS**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**

questions.question: Complete digestion of carbohydrates, proteins and fats takes place in the:
questions.solution:
__
 
• The breakdown of carbohydrates, proteins and fats occurs in the **duodenum region of the small intestine.__**
 
• Small intestine is distinguishable into **__three__** regions:

 
• ‘U’ shaped **duodenum**
 
• A long coiled middle portion **jejunum**
 
• **A highly coiled ileum**.
